title.narrative: Supporting Clean Cooking Solutions in Central and East Africa

description.narrative: The clean cooking sector is gaining traction in some countries of East and Central Africa, but it remains fragmented and underfunded. The dominating use of low-efficiency biomass cooking solutions comes with major negative environmental, socio-economic, health and gender impacts. Significant additional financing and policy efforts in the region are required to reach universal access to clean cooking by 2030.The Action intends to contribute to increasing and accelerating the access to affordable, clean and sustainable cooking solutions (high-tier cooking solutions) in East and Central Africa. The Action will foster clean cooking business development with coaching, financial partnership brokering (finance catalyst) and innovative financial solutions for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) including manufacturers, distributors and importers of clean cooking solutions. More particularly, it will offer results-based-finance and thematic grants to support and accelerate market development and innovation. It will also expand the portfolio of finance institutions to clean cooking through training, sector-specific tools and de-risking mechanisms, like guarantees and credit lines where blending will be possible. It will strengthen the regulatory and market framework by supporting regional dialogue and coordination of policies and plans through platforms, networks of task forces, and by promoting regional performance standards and reduced tariffs barriers, contributing to stronger clean cooking strategies and facilitated international trade of clean cooking solutions. The Action is fully aligned with regional and national policies and strategies. It will build on on-going activities, more particularly, Europe (EU) and EU Member States¿ funded programmes in the region. It is intended to improve, adapt and replicate successful approaches, to selected countries for a possible future extension at full regional scale. This Action will contribute to the regional priority area 3 of the MIP ¿Green Transition¿ and to its specific objective 2 ¿Support the development of an efficient, sustainable and resilient African energy sector¿. The action will also actively contribute to the pledge of the Clean Cooking Declaration of Paris (2024) to make clean cooking a priority and enhance the efforts toward achieving universal access for all.The action will contribute to affordable and clean energy access for cooking (SDG7), climate mitigation (SDG13), forest conservation (SDG15), gender equality, including in entrepreneurship (SDG5), health, more particularly of women and girls (SDG3), and sustainable cities (SDG11).
